citeAs: Rohatgi, Shaurya, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, and Min-Yen Kan. (2023). The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics.
creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan (National University of Singapore; Pennsylvania State University)
description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to support open scientific research in computational linguistics. It contains 73,285 papers published from 1952 to September 2022 and provides metadata, PDF files, structured full texts, citation graph information, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
name: ACL OCL
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most fields are collected automatically by crawling ACL Anthology PDFs and metadata, extracting structured full text with GROBID, extracting figures with PDFFigures, linking papers to Semantic Scholar via its Graph API, and automatically detecting language and predicted topic labels with machine methods.
rai:dataBiases: The corpus is limited to peer-reviewed and open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology, so it does not include other sources beyond the ACL Anthology. The paper also notes linguistic disparity in coverage, with many languages underrepresented in the ACL Anthology and thus in ACL OCL.
rai:dataCollection: The authors designed crawlers to fetch all PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, removed PDF files longer than 50 pages, processed PDFs for structured full-text extraction, extracted figures and tables, and enriched records with information fetched from Semantic Scholar's API.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Certain fields are only valid for a portion of papers; for example, only 16.8% of OCL papers have arXiv_paper_id. The authors also report extraction failures and omissions in full texts, including missing sections, missing footnotes, and undetected figures and tables.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data consist of ACL Anthology website metadata and PDF files for papers hosted in the ACL Anthology, supplemented with information from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Document analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: ACL OCL is limited to peer-reviewed, open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology and is therefore not comprehensive beyond that source. Full-text quality is affected by PDF extraction errors, and the corpus is largely unlabeled for task-specific annotations.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset excludes PDF files longer than 50 pages, converts PDFs into structured full text in S2ORC-JSON format, stores figures separately from textual data, adds automatically detected language and predicted topic fields, and releases model-predicted silver topic labels together with OCL.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files are passed through GROBID for full-text extraction; the output is formatted in S2ORC-JSON schema. Figures and tables are extracted using PDFFigures, papers are linked to Semantic Scholar Academic Graph through its Graph API, and language is detected from title and abstract using a public language detection toolkit.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing papers newly added to the ACL Anthology, identified by monitoring URL changes. The authors also state they plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus is intended to advance open research, reproducibility, and sustainable progress in computational linguistics by providing accessible and standardized scholarly data resources.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses include observing temporal topic trends in computational linguistics, metadata analysis, bibliographic research, document-level information extraction, related work generation, multimodal research using figures, topic-aided tasks, scientific assistant building, knowledge graph construction, and historical language change analysis.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID for PDF full-text extraction; PDFFigures for figure extraction; Semantic Scholar Graph API for metadata and citation linking; a public language detection toolkit (langdetect) for language detection; and trained topic classification models including BART-large-MNLI, SciBERT, and SPECTER for predicted topic labels.
